guarantees.claim: When none of the error condition signals (err_swsequence, err_modestrength, err_prefix, err_entropy_ready) are asserted, err is driven to {valid=0, code=ErrNone, info=0}.
If err_swsequence is true, err is driven with valid=1, code=ErrSwCmdSequence, and info containing {5'h0, {err_swsequence, err_modestrength, err_prefix}, 5'h0, stL, 2'b0, sw_cmd_i}.
If err_swsequence is false and err_modestrength is true, err is driven with valid=1, code=ErrUnexpectedModeStrength, and info containing cfg_mode_i and cfg_strength_i.
If err_swsequence and err_modestrength are false and err_prefix is true, err is driven with valid=1 and code=ErrIncorrectFunctionName.
If all higher-priority error conditions are false and err_entropy_ready is true, err is driven with valid=1, code=ErrSwHashingWithoutEntropyReady, and info containing kmac_en_i and cfg_entropy_ready.

assumptions.claim: The error condition inputs (err_swsequence, err_modestrength, err_prefix, err_entropy_ready) must always be clean Boolean (0 or 1) and not X or Z.
assumptions.risk: If any input is X, the priority case may resolve unpredictably, possibly driving a valid error with malformed info or incorrectly suppressing a real error.

uncertain_points.claim: Only four error sources (sw sequence, mode strength, prefix, entropy ready) are encoded into the err output. Other potential error conditions in kmac_errchk (e.g., checksum, state machine faults, invalid configurations) may exist but are not visible in this chunk.
uncertain_points.risk: A genuine error not connected to these four signals would be silently ignored, violating fault coverage or safety requirements.
